newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica needs schedule to lift fx controls - Santam.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica needs schedule to lift fx controls - Santam.

text.p: South African insurer Santam Ltd on Friday urged the government to prepare a schedule outlining its plans to abolish exchange controls.
Santam chairman Marinus Daling said in the group's latest annual report that without such a schedule, "the markets will continue to speculate against the rand to the detriment of the economy."
Daling said that exchange controls made it difficult for South African companies to compete on an equal footing globally.
"If we want to compete with the rest of the world, it is imperative that exchange control be abolished, sooner rather than later," he said.
"We do realise that the low level of reserves militates against this. It is, however, important that a schedule be prepared, setting out government's plans for abolishing exchange control."
Daling said that the depreciation of the rand should offer new export opportunities while also supporting the level of foreign exchange reserves.
He added that the greatest challenge facing Santam was ensuring continued good results in the face of weaker economic growth and persistently high levels of crime.
He said this should be achievable through a greater concentration on the quality of underwriting, the introduction and use of data bases and information technology.
Claims for weather-related natural disasters appeared to be on the increase and the effect of this on group results could not be predicted.
"However, we do have adequate reinsurance, which shields the company's results," Daling said.
